children.text: The coastal walkway along Roxas Boulevard is where Manila's world-famous sunset comes into view. Stretching from Dolomite Beach along the seaside promenade to the Mall of Asia waterfront, it's the best-loved place for a walk at dusk.
Manila Bay is a natural harbor about
190km

around, with Corregidor Island guarding its mouth, making it one of Southeast Asia's most important ports for centuries. In the 16th century, Spanish galleons set sail from here for Acapulco in Mexico, and in

, the Battle of Manila Bay saw the American fleet defeat the Spanish fleet here. For travelers, Manila Bay is above all a "sea of sunsets" — as the sun sets over the wide bay behind the mountains of the Bataan Peninsula, the whole sky turns orange and pink, a scene that has become Manila's signature view.

Most travelers head for the waterfront along Roxas Boulevard, which runs from Ermita and Malate in Manila City into Pasay City. The palm-lined seaside promenade known as the Baywalk stretches for about
2km
, and between the US Embassy and the Manila Yacht Club breakwater lies Dolomite Beach, an artificial beach about
long created in

. To the south, the reclaimed land of Pasay City and Parañaque City (Bay City) is home to the SM Mall of Asia seaside promenade and large casino resort complexes, so the evening can carry on from the sunset to night views and shopping.
Most of today's shoreline is reclaimed land. Roxas Boulevard is a coastal road laid out in the
under American urban planner Daniel Burnham's plan for Manila; once known as Dewey Boulevard, it took its current name in
and runs about
7.6km
from Rizal Park to Parañaque. In
December 2008
, the Supreme Court of the Philippines ordered 13 government agencies to restore Manila Bay to water quality safe for swimming (Class SB), and a large-scale cleanup has been underway since
. Meanwhile, in
August 2023
the president suspended all reclamation projects in Manila Bay, but some have been allowed to move forward again after review, so the coastline may keep changing.

To be honest, Manila Bay isn't a swimming beach. Water quality cleanup efforts are ongoing after decades of pollution, and swimming and water sports at the beach are currently banned. Instead, enjoy strolling in the sea breeze at dusk and soaking in the lively atmosphere of local families and couples who gather here.

Since it connects on foot with Intramuros, Rizal Park, and the National Museum, it makes a great final stop for a day of downtown Manila sightseeing. Recommended for travelers who love photography, and for families and couples who want a relaxed evening walk.

blocks.title: Watch the sunset at the Baywalk

children.text: You can see the sunset from anywhere along the Roxas Boulevard coastal walkway, but the area around the Manila Yacht Club and the western end of Rizal Park have especially good views. Arrive
30 minutes
before sunset to claim a spot on the breakwater.
An artificial beach covered in white dolomite sand, crowded at dusk with families out for the evening and people taking photos. Admission is free, but it's closed on Thursdays for cleaning.

blocks.title: Mall of Asia and SM by the Bay

children.text: At SM by the Bay, a promenade stretching about
1.5km
along the waterfront behind SM Mall of Asia, you can watch the sun go down beyond the
-tall MOA Eye Ferris wheel. The amusement ride area opens at
1–3 PM
and stays open until around midnight. Every year on Saturday nights in
February–March
, the Philippine International Pyromusical Competition is held just offshore, and a big fireworks display lights up the same waters on New Year's Eve.
Dinner cruises that circle the inner bay at sunset depart from a pier near the Cultural Center of the Philippines (CCP) complex, and many packages last
1.5–3 hours
with a meal and live music included. Since Sun Cruises, long the leading operator, closed in
, operators and departure points have changed often, so check the dates of recent reviews on booking sites before you choose.
Seaside Market (Seaside Dampa) on Macapagal Boulevard in Pasay City,
10–15 minutes

by car from Mall of Asia, is a paluto-style dining strip: you buy shrimp, crab, clams, and fish by weight at the seafood market, then have one of the neighboring restaurants cook them. Each restaurant charges its own cooking fee, so agree on the cooking style and the fee before buying your seafood.
A marine theme park on the waterfront behind the Quirino Grandstand in Rizal Park, with an oceanarium, a jellyfish exhibit, a penguin habitat, and a sea lion show. It's open
10 AM–6 PM
on weekdays and
9 AM–6 PM
on weekends and holidays, and shows usually start at
and
. With kids, a good plan is to explore in the afternoon and then watch the sunset from the waterfront right outside.

After dark, head south along Roxas Boulevard to Entertainment City in Parañaque City, where the lights of casino resorts such as Solaire, City of Dreams, and Okada Manila reflect on the water. In front of Okada Manila is The Fountain, a multicolored musical fountain said to be the largest in the world; check the resort's announcements for show times.

blocks.title: Malate Church and Rajah Sulayman Plaza

children.text: In the Malate district across from the Baywalk stands Malate Church (Our Lady of Remedies Parish), founded in
and rebuilt in stone in
. Rajah Sulayman Plaza in front of the church has a statue of Rajah Sulayman and a fountain, both built in
, making it a nice spot to take in the church and the sea together at dusk.

From Clark International Airport (CRK), Genesis runs P2P buses to the PITX terminal in southern Manila, taking about
2.5–3 hours
, with fares of
(regular Deluxe or JoyBus). The route launched in
March 2026
and runs 8 times a day in both directions. From PITX, take LRT Line 1 from the station of the same name to UN Avenue or Pedro Gil station, or take a Grab and reach Roxas Boulevard in
20–40 minutes
Get off LRT Line 1 at UN Avenue, Pedro Gil, or Quirino (Malate) station and walk west for
10–15 minutes
to reach the Roxas Boulevard waterfront. Fares are about
. For Mall of Asia, walk about
2km
from LRT Line 1's Redemptorist-Aseana station, which opened in
November 2024
, or transfer at LRT Line 1 EDSA station or MRT Line 3 Taft Avenue station to a jeepney or bus bound for Mall of Asia.
Many jeepneys and city buses run along Roxas Boulevard, so take one marked "Roxas Blvd" or "MOA." The jeepney base fare is about
. Around sunset it is commuting time and vehicles get very crowded, so Grab is recommended if you have a lot of luggage.
From Intramuros, the National Museum, or Rizal Park, it's a
10–20-minute
walk to the coast. Walking the coastal path to Dolomite Beach takes about
15 minutes
from Rizal Park.
To the south, Roxas Boulevard connects with the Manila–Cavite Expressway (CAVITEX) in Parañaque, making it easy to reach from Cavite. Around sunset,
5–8 PM
, commuter traffic is extremely heavy, so arrive early. For parking, use the paid lots around Rizal Park, UN Avenue, Manila Ocean Park, the Manila Hotel, and Robinsons Place Manila.
For the best sunsets, come in the
November–April
dry season. Clear skies with just the right amount of cloud bring out vivid red sunsets, and
December–February
in particular has cool sea breezes that make for pleasant walks. According to climate normals from the Port Area station on the bayfront,
January–April
sees only 3–4 rainy days a month, and daytime highs rise from about
in
January
to about
in
April–May
. Sunset is earliest in
late November–early December
at about

in

in
June–July
March–May
is hot during the day, but evening walks are still quite comfortable.
During the
June–October
rainy season, rain clouds often roll in during the afternoon and block the sun. Still, dramatic sunsets sometimes appear right after the rain clears. When typhoons hit in
July–September
, high waves pound the coast and Roxas Boulevard can flood, so stay away from the breakwater. On days with a strong southwest monsoon (habagat), waves can wash over the walkway.

Weekend and holiday evenings draw huge crowds of local families. On the SM Mall of Asia waterfront, the Philippine International Pyromusical Competition, where companies from different countries compete, is held on Saturday nights every
February–March
(in
, from
February 21–March 21
). During the
December
Christmas season, Roxas Boulevard and Mall of Asia are decked out in lights, and on New Year's Eve you can watch fireworks all along the coast.

If you want to watch the Manila Bay sunset from your room, choose a hotel on the bay side of Roxas Boulevard. The Manila Hotel, opened in
, and the Diamond Hotel, midway along Roxas Boulevard, have long been known for their bay views, and sea-view rooms cost about
a night. The large resorts in Parañaque's Entertainment City (from about
a night) let you enjoy casinos, shows, and restaurants all in one place. On a tighter budget, hotels in the
range in the heart of Malate are also within a
10-minute
walk of the waterfront.
For food, Aristocrat, a Filipino restaurant on Roxas Boulevard that opened in

, is a long-standing favorite known for its chicken barbecue and Java rice. If you love seafood, try the Dampa food stalls near Mall of Asia, where you buy shrimp, crab, and fish and have them grilled or cooked in chili sauce or garlic butter. Grilled corn, isaw (chicken-intestine skewers), and buko juice from the walkway vendors are also great while waiting for the sunset. Malate has several Korean restaurants as well.
For a meal with a sea view, Harbor View (opened in

), on the pier in front of Rizal Park's south entrance, is a long-standing choice that specializes in grilled seafood; it gets busy at sunset and on weekends, so it's best to book ahead. Aristocrat's flagship on Roxas Boulevard, at the corner of San Andres Street, is open 24 hours, making it a handy stop after a late-night walk. Cooking fees at Seaside Dampa run about
per kg depending on the restaurant and the dish, and many reviews mention being overcharged, so be sure to check the scale reading and your bill.
Check the sunset time with a weather app and arrive at least
30 minutes
early. Don't miss the "magic hour" — the
10–20 minutes
after sunset when the sky turns deepest red.
Dolomite Beach stops admitting new visitors at
6 PM
, so it's safest to enter before
. Hours can change, so check announcements from the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR).
For photos, framing palm-tree silhouettes on the breakwater in the foreground adds atmosphere. If you have a telephoto lens, try lining up anchored ships with the setting sun.
The sea breeze is strong enough to blow away hats. Mosquito repellent makes the evening walk much more comfortable.
Vendors and jeepneys take cash only, so bring small bills.
Roxas Boulevard gets extremely congested at dusk, so if you have an evening appointment, allow extra travel time or take the LRT.
Sunset cruises often sell out on weekends, so book online 1–2 days ahead.
Dolomite Beach's entrance is on the US Embassy side and opens at
6 AM
. For restrooms, it's easiest to use Manila Ocean Park, Robinsons Place Manila, or nearby fast-food restaurants.
At Manila Ocean Park, online bundle tickets from the official website or booking apps (from
) are much cheaper than at the on-site ticket counter, and children 2 feet (about 61cm) tall or under get in free.
If you'll ride the LRT several times, buy a beep card (a stored-value transit card) at a station to skip the ticket lines; fares are also slightly cheaper than with single-journey tickets.
Swimming and water play are banned in Manila Bay due to water quality issues. Enjoy the sand only, and avoid even dipping your hands or feet in the water.
Pickpockets are present during the crowded sunset hours. They often target phones and bags while people are focused on taking photos.
Avoid the quiet breakwater, the Roxas Boulevard underpasses, and dark park areas late at night — take a Grab instead.
During typhoons or strong monsoon winds, waves can surge over the breakwater onto the walkway, so don't get too close to the water's edge.
Some people on the walkway push flowers or trinkets on you and then ask for money — don't accept them, and decline politely.
After heavy rain or the southwest monsoon, trash carried down by rivers washes up on the beach, and parts of Roxas Boulevard can flood. In
August 2026
, about 60 tons of trash were cleared from Dolomite Beach alone.

Manila Bay's beach is for strolling and watching the sunset. Swimming is banned until water quality meets standards, so if a beach vacation is your goal, choose another beach such as Batangas or Palawan.
